learningObjective: Compute the per-rank bandwidth term of a ring-AllReduce for a tensor of S bytes across N ranks.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a ring-AllReduce of a payload of S bytes across N ranks, each rank sends and receives approximately 2·(N-1)/N · S bytes over the bandwidth-limited term, decomposed as ReduceScatter [(N-1)/N · S] followed by AllGather [(N-1)/N · S].
conditions: The interconnect between neighbors in the ring has effective bandwidth BW (bytes/s).
Latency term α·(N-1) per phase is negligible relative to the bandwidth term for large S.
The payload is evenly divided into N chunks.
nonImplications: Does not imply that AllReduce moves 2·S bytes per rank; the (N-1)/N factor reflects that each chunk is skipped by its owner rank.
Does not imply the cost scales as N; the bandwidth term is nearly independent of N (approaches 2S).

sourceMappings.locator: §3 cost analysis of collective primitives used by the partitioner

misconceptions.claim: Ring-AllReduce sends N·S bytes per rank because each rank forwards the full tensor to each of the other N-1 peers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The tensor is split into N chunks; each chunk traverses the ring once during reduce-scatter and once during all-gather, so the per-rank bandwidth cost is ~2(N-1)/N · S, not N·S.

misconceptions.claim: Ring-AllReduce is bandwidth-bound with cost S/BW per rank because the tensor is only transmitted once.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is transmitted twice through the ring (reduce-scatter phase and all-gather phase), giving ~2(N-1)/N · S bytes per rank.

misconceptions.claim: Tree-AllReduce and ring-AllReduce have identical bandwidth costs; only their latency terms differ.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Naive tree-AllReduce broadcasts back the full reduced tensor, whereas ring interleaves ReduceScatter+AllGather so that each chunk moves once per phase. Their bandwidth and latency terms differ.

performanceScenarios: Gradient AllReduce for a 1 GB gradient bucket across 8 ranks: bandwidth term ≈ 2·(7/8)·1 GB ≈ 1.75 GB per rank.
